_about: The modern on-screen controls: Magic Rampage's inset pad, laid out for Magic Portals. The numbers of the layout, the hit
rule, the tuning grids and the art's margins, read by game/sim/Controls (planning step 180; the design is
docs/planning/2026-10-15-modern-controls.md, sections 1, 3.1 and 4.2). The CLASSIC controls are not here: they are ui.json's
hud block, untouched, and sim/Controls forwards to them.
Every number says where it came from. `_source` is an array of lines, each naming the key it is about; `_guess` is true
where the number is the port's own decision and not a measurement (a per-key `_guess_<key>` where one object holds both).
A test walks this tree and fails on a number with neither. The tags (docs/planning/2026-10-15-modern-controls.md 1.1):
DECODED = Penumbra's docs/spec/42-magic-rampage-screenpad.md (another repository, read only; its line numbers are cited as
`spec 42 l.N`), MEASURED = a tool run on a file, OWNER = the owner's decisions of 2026-10-15, PORT = a decision of this port.
Units: Magic Rampage's reference is 1280x720 and is converted BY HEIGHT: a px here is view height / reference.height_px units
(256 / 720 = 0.35556 at the port's view, 2.8125 px to a unit: ui.json _about). Nothing below is in units except where its name says so.
sim/Controls.LoadRules reads this file STRICTLY: every key below that does not begin with an underscore must be there with its
own type and range, or the file is refused and the run plays the classic controls. Unknown keys are ignored, so a later step
may add one. That includes `layout.presets.<name>.margin_bottom_px`: every look names its own (it used to fall back to
`layout.margin_px.bottom`, and a misspelt key then loaded cleanly at the shared 44 px, a pair drawn at the wrong height).
_source: clearance_px 16: DECODED spec 42 l.121: collapseButtons moves a pad button while `a.isOverlapping(b, 16 px)`. It is the adjust
screen's overlap rule (design 3.3), read by CTL-11 and kept here so the layout's numbers live in one file.
height_px 720: DECODED spec 42 l.48: the layer file's 1280x720 reference; every px below is in it, converted by height.
version 2: PORT. The number of the default arrangement (design 2.4). Whoever changes a default place bumps kLayoutVersion in
sim/Controls.hpp and this number together, so a saved move that was made against another arrangement is dropped, not misapplied.
1 was the walk arrows grouped at the bottom left (planning step 180); 2 is walk_left in the bottom-left and walk_right in the
bottom-right corner (planning step 186: the OWNER's decision of 2026-10-16, after he saw the layout on his screen: 'moving stick should
not be only on the left side. you should put one button to the left and one to the right like the classic ones'). A controls.json
saved at layout 1 keeps its size and opacity and drops its moves.
gap_px 32: DECODED spec 42 l.78: 32 px between neighbours (the two arrows; restart and pause).
box_px 128: DECODED spec 42 l.77-78: the sprites are 128 px; the sprite box is the layout unit, flush at its edge.
corner_box_factor 0.9: the VALUE is DECODED spec 42 l.77 (the pause is 0.9 x the pad scale); the APPLICATION to restart and
clear-portals as well is PORT.
corner_min_size 1.0: PORT: a corner button never shrinks below 128 x 0.9 px = 40.96 units, whose solid face is exactly 32.0
units, the classic corner button's size, so a small arrow does not shrink restart, pause or clear.
face_inset 0.109375: MEASURED (Pillow, alpha >= 250, dpad-left/right/frame, 14 px of 128; CTL/mapC_art.md): the solid face is the
box shrunk by this fraction of the box on every side. The art's own transparent margin is art.<tier>.<id>.body_inset.
side 44, top 44, bottom 44: the VALUE is DECODED spec 42 l.78 (44 px from the screen's side edges). The APPLICATION is the
OWNER's of 2026-10-15, 'inset from the corner by the same margin': the same 44 px on both edges of every corner, the bottom
included (Magic Rampage's own bottom row is flush). The margin is to the BOX, never to the visible face (design 1.1).
The three looks (design 1.1, Q3). size is the arrow's scale on Magic Rampage's grid; margin_bottom_px is the arrows' margin to the
bottom edge. Chosen FROM THE CENSUS (design 1.9): at the default the arrows' top must sit below the character's row (206 units).
uniform 0.7 / 44 px: the owner's 'same margin' literally, arrows' top 208.50, the recommended default.
balanced 0.8 / 34 px: a larger arrow, 10 px under the margin at the bottom, arrows' top 207.50.
mr 1.0 / 11 px: Magic Rampage's own arrow size (spec 42 l.74-76), arrows' top 206.58.
size 0.7, margin_bottom_px 44: see presets.
size 0.8, margin_bottom_px 34: see presets.
size 1.0, margin_bottom_px 11: see presets.

layout._default_preset: PORT, design D1/Q3: the look the owner is shown first. One data line to change.
layout._default_arrows: OWNER 2026-10-16 (planning step 186): `split` is walk_left in the bottom-left corner and walk_right in the bottom-right corner, each inset by margin_px.side and the look's bottom margin, as the classic pair stands but inset; `grouped` is the arrangement of planning step 180 (both at the bottom left, 32 px apart), kept as an alternative that a capture or a test asks for with `--controls modern,arrows=grouped`: it is never saved. The looks (presets) are orthogonal to it.

_source: seam_px 32: PORT (equal to layout.gap_px): a gap of at most this between two boxes is split at its middle (design 1.4 rule 2).
edge_reach_px 48: PORT (= the 44 px margin + 4 px): a side whose box edge is within this of the view's (safe-area) edge extends
to the edge, so the strip beside a box is the control's and a missed corner tap is not a portal (design 1.4 rule 3).
walk_left, walk_right, restart, pause, clear_portals: PORT, 0 each. Growth toward the world, per control. Magic Rampage grows its
touch areas 4 to 8 steps of 16 px (spec 42 l.80); 0 is right for a mouse and for a thumb on a margin (the owner's answer Q0 of
2026-10-15: desktop AND touch, growth 0 in the data; a thumb's growth is a later, MEASURED data change, and then the census of
tests/golden/controls_census.json is re-run before the list is signed). 16 px of growth costs 8, 14 or 16 levels' recorded shots
at uniform, balanced or mr (design 1.9).
act_on release: PORT, design D11 and Q8: restart, pause and clear-portals act on the RELEASE inside their hit rectangle after a
press inside it, which is the original's own Button rule (MagicPortalsLayer.cpp 8741); the classic style keeps its recorded
deviation, the press. `press` is the other value.
two_contacts true: OWNER. The 2026-10-15 answer to Q0 was BOTH desktop and touch, and on 2026-10-16 he answered yes to amending the
one-pointer rule (planning step 191, CTL-14): under the modern controls a second finger reaches the controls and the world through the
layer's one pointer path, so a thumb held on an arrow keeps walking while another finger shoots, aims or pans. The classic style never
reads this key and stays one pointer; with one finger down nothing differs from before. A desktop mouse is one finger, so on a
desktop this changes nothing a player can see; a second finger exists only on a touch device (the engine's Android backend) or in a
replayed tick, and no touch build exists yet. `--controls modern,contacts=one|two` overrides it for a run.
min 0.4, max 1.4, step 0.1: DECODED spec 42 l.75-76: the pad scale, 0.4 to 1.4 in steps of 0.1, eleven values; the tuning keeps whole
steps and divides once (design 3.1), so a chain of steps ends exactly on the limits.
min 0.2, max 1.8, step 0.2: DECODED spec 42 l.87: a multiplier, 0.2 to 1.8 in steps of 0.2, nine values.
default 1.0: DECODED spec 42 l.86 (screenPadTransparency, 1.0).
base_alpha_byte 120: DECODED + MEASURED: ui.json hud.opacity.alpha_byte, the classic controls' alpha, which the modern byte
MULTIPLIES and does not replace, so toggling the style does not change the brightness. Kept here as the number a test
compares with ui.json's.
idle_scale 1.0: PORT. Magic Rampage's own base alpha is min(0.25 / s^2, 0.25) (spec 42 l.89): 0.53 here would reproduce its ghost
look (0.25 / 0.4706). 1.0 leaves the classic byte unchanged (Q10).
boost_byte 38: PORT, a guess: a held arrow or button draws this many bytes brighter (Penumbra's pressed look is +0.15 of 255 = 38.25).
Magic Rampage's own pressed look is a flash to opaque white (spec 42 l.90, 'likely'). Read by CTL-7.
size_over_box 3.125: PORT, derived: the classic ring is 200 units over a 64-unit pad (ui.json hud.pads.ring.size_units over
hud.pads.size_units); the modern ring is that many boxes across, so it follows the arrow's size.
margin_units 8: PORT: 1-21's hint text (camera.json hint) ends this far inside the view's right edge when the pair pushes it right
(design 1.6).

_about: Which picture each control is drawn with, per tier, and the transparent margin that picture carries (design 1.3, 4.2). A tier's
file is searched for in its own place: mr = reference/magic-rampage/controls (gitignored, never committed); original = the
original's own sprite folder, through the layer's menuImage; generated = the pad art the port draws itself (sim/PadArt) into prisms.
The first tier whose picture is present is used; a tier's `body_inset` is the fraction of its picture that is transparent on each side.
A `generated` entry's body_inset is at most 0.25 (sim/PadArt draws no more, and the loader refuses a value that would load and draw nothing).

_about: THE OPTIONS SCREEN and the main menu's entry to it (planning step 185; design 2.3), read by sim/Options.LoadRules, STRICTLY and apart
from the rest of this file: sim/Controls.LoadRules does not read this block, and a typo in it makes the modern controls unavailable
with one error line (design D9), never a classic run. An ENHANCEMENT: the original has no options screen, so the screen is the
credits' own background and back button (ui.json credits, read by sim/Credits) and flat quads and words in the original's font.
Places are fractions of the screen as ui.json's main_menu is; sizes are units (2.8125 px a unit at 1280x720); a colour is r, g, b, a
bytes. Every number here is the port's own decision, so each object says so: the owner's eyes, not a measurement, settle the look.

(clearance_px, DECODED spec 42 l.119, 16 px): Back's place is FIXED - its left edge is the layout's side margin from the safe rectangle's left and its
top is the layout's top margin, plus the LARGEST corner box (size 1.4), plus this gap, from the safe rectangle's top - so it clears clear_portals' box by

49 to 54 px tall, so 19.6 to 21.6 units. alpha_byte 255: PORT.
The words are the VALUE: n / 10 for the size, n / 5 for the opacity, one decimal ('0.7', '1.0'), digits and the point only - the tiles are the minus and the
plus. The widest, '0.4', is 40.8 units to its last glyph's edge, inside the 46.36 between the two tiles' faces (a test measures all twenty with the real font).
alpha_byte 90: PORT, design 3.3.1 'alpha 90/255': a tile at its limit, and Restore with no move to clear, is drawn at this and does nothing.
tile_rgba and unlocked_rgba: PORT, the last tier of a widget's picture (no Magic Rampage file, no drawn glyph): a flat quad on the widget's face, light
on the dark backdrop; the lock is the red one while it is unlocked.
outline_thickness_units 0.7, outline_alpha_byte 110, outline_swing_byte 70, outline_period_ticks 48: DECODED/adapted from design 3.3.2 (Magic Rampage wiggles the
boxes, B 2.2; no rotation is needed): a thin outline round each control's box, breathing between alpha 40 and 180 as a triangle over 48 ticks - the state's own
ticks, never the wall clock.
hit_frame_alpha_byte 34 (0x22) and hit_frame_thickness_units 0.5: DECODED spec 42 l.80 (Magic Rampage draws the hit rectangles too), design 3.3.2: each control's hit rectangle
as a faint frame, from LayOut's own rectangles.
guide_thickness_units 0.7: PORT, design 3.3.2: a thin line across the preview at the character's row (census.character_row_units).
held_outline_thickness_units 1.0 and held_outline_alpha_byte 255 (planning step 193, CTL-12): PORT, design 3.3.2 ('1 unit and solid while held'): the outline of the
control a finger is dragging, in place of the breathing one - thicker and not fading, so the player sees which one the pointer has.
step_units 0.5 (planning step 193, CTL-12): PORT. A drag moves the control toward the pointer in steps of at most this many units, the x component first and then
the y, and refuses a step that would meet another control (grown by clearance_px) or a widget, so the control cannot jump over a neighbour at any speed of the
pointer; the step that is refused is bisected, so it stops within a tenth of a unit of the clearance (a move is kept to a tenth, Controls::Tuning::kMoveSnap) and, for a
drag blocked along one axis or sliding along one face, a move of 1 unit a tick and one of 40 end on the same place (a diagonal drag that ends inside an obstacle can
end beside it or above it depending on how coarsely the pointer is sampled, though nothing is jumped: planning step 193, recorded deviation 2). A step must be more
than the tenth, or the walk would stand still in the rounding; an obstacle is wider
than a step, or a neighbour could be stepped over (the loader refuses a step under 0.2 or over 8: the smallest box is 18.2 units across).

_about: The eight pictures of the seven widgets (the lock has one per state), each through the tiers the five controls use (design 4.2): Magic Rampage's own, read at run time
from the folder `editor` beside the controls' (tools/art/make_mr_controls.py --stage editor), a glyph the game draws itself (sim/PadArt) and writes into its scratch
directory, and last a flat quad. A file name is a bare file name (Controls::IsBareFileName), and no two pictures share one, in this block or with the controls'
generated pictures and the Options gear. Every picture is drawn so that its body fills the widget's face (Controls::DrawRect): a picture with a bigger margin
is drawn bigger and the faces stay the same size.
